thread:
Maya Chen: FYI customer (healthtech) just sent a list of audit asks: signed audit events, per-key KMS id in event, 7 years retention for evidence, and an SLA for delivery of audit bundles within 48h. They want this in the contract (BAA + SOC2).
Theo Rivera: do we currently sign events or provide tamper-evident bundles? I think we have tamper logs + append-only storage, but not cryptographic signing of exported bundles.
Jordan Patel: we emit structured audit records to our audit topic (kafka), with fields: actor, action, resource, timestamp, result, request_id. No kms_key_id field right now.
Maya Chen: they explicitly asked for kms_key_id (customer-managed CMK) referenced in each event for encryption context. Also want proof that logs were generated before any retention deletion.
Priya Kapoor (Legal): if this goes in the contract we need deterministic validation steps and an SLA. We should propose a clear acceptance criteria: sample bundle format + verification tool + retention guarantee.
Theo Rivera: proposal sketch: 1) extend event schema with optional kms_key_id and envelope_signature fields; 2) provide a signed bundle export endpoint that returns a gzipped newline-delimited JSON plus a detached signature (ed25519) generated by our HSM; 3) add a signed manifest with hashes for each event.
Jordan Patel: implementation notes: adding kms_key_id is straightforward (producer side), envelope_signature requires us to sign either each event or the manifest. Per-event signing at write time will add latency. Manifest+bundle signing during export keeps write path fast.
Maya Chen: customer insisted on ability to verify signature with a public key and to confirm the signing time. They also asked for RFC-compliant timestamp formats and canonical JSON before signing.
Theo Rivera: example manifest format I mocked: ```
{
  "bundle_id": "bndl-20260201-01",
  "created_at": "2026-02-01T18:22:10Z",
  "events_count": 432,
  "event_hash_algo": "sha256",
  "manifest_signature_alg": "ed25519",
  "events_sha256": ["<hex>", "<hex>"]
}
```
Jordan Patel: ops questions: where do we store the private signing key? Customer prefers us to sign with an HSM-backed key; for private deployments they might manage the key themselves. For hosted customers we can sign with Redwood-managed HSM and publish the public key per-tenant.
Maya Chen: retention + SLA: they want 7 years retention for evidence and a contractual SLA of 99.9% availability for the bundle export endpoint and 48h maximum delivery for on-demand audit bundles. That has infra cost implications.
Priya Kapoor (Legal): suggest we map this to three contract clauses: evidence retention window & deletion policies, signed-evidence delivery SLA (48h), and acceptance test (we deliver 1 sample signed bundle within X days). Also add liability cap language tied to deliberate tampering.
Theo Rivera: vuln/ops: generating manifest/signatures creates an additional attack surface. We need IID for signing service, rotation plan, and key access audits. Also need to ensure the event pipeline is immutable between generation and manifest creation (e.g., use append-only storage + monotonic offsets).
Jordan Patel: quick action items: 1) add schema change PR to include "kms_key_id" (owner @Jordan) 2) design signed-bundle export prototype (owner @Theo) 3) ops runbook + HSM key management checklist (owner @Maya) 4) legal to draft contract language (owner @Priya).
Maya Chen: timeline: customer expects an initial design review this week and a contract term proposal next week. I'll coordinate with Customer Success to set expectations.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: created ticket SEC-1129 for signed-bundles feature (assignee: Theo Rivera).
Priya Kapoor (Legal): please include sample acceptance tests in the PR so I can attach to the contract. e.g., verify manifest signature using the public key, check event count matches, validate canonical JSON hash.
Theo Rivera: noted. I'll add a simple verification script example and a canonicalization step (RFC8785 JSON Canonicalization).
Maya Chen: thanks — let's sync after the design review. :thumbsup:
